whatFailed: GET /v2/slots (cal-api-version 2024-09-04) on a seated event type returned 200 with per-slot seat data named seatsBooked / seatsRemaining / seatsTotal (plus bookingUid), while the endpoint's own published 200-response description promises the seat count under the name attendeesCount, which appears nowhere in the response.

docClaim.quote: For seated slots each object will have attendeesCount and bookingUid properties.
docClaim.doc: .truecourse/specs/sources/cal.com-docs/docs/api-reference/v2/slots/get-available-time-slots-for-an-event-type.md line 237; the same sentence is generated from the tested tree at apps/api/v2/src/modules/slots/slots-2024-09-04/controllers/slots.controller.ts:205 and is committed at docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json:5431

observed: Step 1 booked a 4th seat on event type 102 at 2050-09-08T14:00Z (201). Step 2's GET /v2/slots returned {"data":{"2050-09-08":[{"start":"...T13:00:00.000Z","seatsBooked":0,"seatsRemaining":10,"seatsTotal":10}, ... {"start":"...T14:00:00.000Z","seatsBooked":4,"seatsRemaining":6,"seatsTotal":10,"bookingUid":"ptL2busPDT5RbZRbp5Pmi9"}, ...]},"status":"success"}. The seat arithmetic is correct and richer than the doc promises; only the field name attendeesCount is missing. bookingUid is present only on the two slots that already have a booking, not on every seated slot. The request sent cal-api-version 2024-09-04, a version Cal.diy does ship (packages/platform/constants/api.ts:60), so the version-downgrade systemic cause does not apply here.
impact: Anyone integrating against the published v2 slots reference reads the seat count as slot.attendeesCount and gets undefined for every seated slot; the correct names (seatsBooked, seatsRemaining, seatsTotal) appear nowhere in the entire snapshotted cal.com docs corpus, so the docs give a reader no way to find them. No data loss, but a guaranteed broken seated-slots integration written from the docs.

rootCause.explanation: The @DocsResponse decorator on getAvailableSlots carries a hand-written prose description (line 205) claiming seated slot objects have attendeesCount and bookingUid, and a hand-written schema (lines 207-258) whose oneOf branches declare only start (default/time format) or start plus end (range format). Neither the prose nor the schema is derived from the DTOs that actually shape the response. The real emitter is apps/api/v2/src/modules/slots/slots-2024-09-04/services/slots-output.service.ts:91-104 (getAvailableTimeSlotSeated) and 188-203 (getAvailableRangeSlotSeated), which return { start, seatsBooked, seatsRemaining: seatsPerTimeslot - seatsBooked, seatsTotal, bookingUid }, matching the typed contract packages/platform/types/slots/slots-2024-09-04/outputs/slots.output.ts:10-26 (SeatedSlot_2024_09_04) and :38-54 (SeatedRangeSlot_2024_09_04), whose @ApiProperty descriptions are correct. The product's own e2e suite pins the emitted shape (apps/api/v2/src/modules/slots/slots-2024-09-04/controllers/e2e/user-event-type-slots.controller.e2e-spec.ts:900-952 asserts seatsBooked/seatsRemaining/seatsTotal), so the behavior is intentional and the prose is the wrong artifact. Because the DocsResponse schema never references SeatedSlot_2024_09_04, the generated docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json inherits both faults: wrong prose and no seat fields in the schema. The fix is to point the DocsResponse schema at the seated DTOs and correct the sentence, not to change the response.

colleagueFinding.note: Does not map to any of the five findings in /Users/musheghgevorgyan/repos/cal.diy/docs/guard-findings.md. The closest is caldiy #4 (adding an attendee to a seated booking is accepted, seat counts go wrong: negative seats left, oversold), but that is a different endpoint and a behavior claim; this failure is purely the response field naming and the seat arithmetic here was internally consistent (seatsTotal 10, seatsBooked 4, seatsRemaining 6, no oversell) on the normal POST /v2/bookings path, which neither confirms nor contradicts #4.

notes: Not an edition-mismatch: the offending doc text lives inside the tested Cal.diy tree itself (slots.controller.ts:205, committed docs/api-reference/v2/openapi.json:5431), the published cal.com page is generated from that same openapi.json, and the seated-slots code is present and works. Not a test-defect either: the scenario encodes the doc sentence verbatim, and the scenario's own note flags that it was authored doc-faithfully in the expectation of going red. Two extra inaccuracies for the doc author, both in the same sentence: (1) `bookingUid` is not on every seated slot object, only on slots that already have a booking, because slots-output.service.ts returns bookingUid: undefined and JSON.stringify drops the key (see the 13:00, 15:00, 15:30, 16:00, 16:30 slots in the evidence); (2) the 200-response schema oneOf declares no seat fields at all in either branch, so even a reader who distrusts the prose cannot recover the right names from the reference. Suggested fix: replace the sentence with 'For seated slots each object also has seatsBooked, seatsRemaining and seatsTotal, and bookingUid when the slot already has a booking', and wire the DocsResponse schema to SeatedSlot_2024_09_04 / SeatedRangeSlot_2024_09_04 so the generated openapi.json stops drifting from the DTOs.
